name: Modern SEO Course
body:
> Course · 2026-10-22

Back to: [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
A video course (4 modules, 17 lessons, about 97 minutes) teaching one agency's system for ranking local businesses in the Google map pack, then building the agency around it. The course sidebar shows it is hosted in the "AI SEO Mastery with Caleb Ulku" Skool group, with modules named The Local SEO Reality Check, Complete Low-Competition Ranking, Core 30 System Introduction, and Client Acquisition Fundamentals.

Core idea: local SEO ranks the [Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile) (GBP), not the website. Google ranks a GBP on proximity (cannot be changed), relevance (topical and geographic, built with content) and trust (quality links and verified listings). Building relevance and trust widens the area where the GBP shows in the top 3. Everything is measured with a grid rank map, and the number that matters is top 3 (green) coverage, because "fourth position or lower is basically invisible."

Module 4 turns from ranking clients to running the agency: getting clients and pricing work so every client is profitable. Its rule matches the rest of the course: show value before you sell.

# Phases (move on only when the rank map says so)
1. Measure first: rank map before any change.
2. Fix the basics with the three-step method (GBP, GBP landing page, verified citations).
3. Add trust: Chamber of Commerce, 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month.
4. If still stuck, build topical relevance with Core 30.
5. Once green coverage hits the target, build geographic relevance (service area, neighborhood and landmark content).

# Threads across all four modules
- The rank map decides every move, and in Module 4 it becomes a free sales tool and the plateau check.
- The GBP is the blueprint for the website (title tag, H1, Core 30 page list and links).
- Consistency of NAP everywhere; do not break what works; client approval first.
- AI speeds up the work but is never trusted blindly (gap analysis, page drafts, marketing content).
- Show value before selling: the gap analysis unlocks the ads system, the free rank map is the networking offer, educational content beats promotion, proposals lead with scope.
- The lobby test returns: a large site ranking 20+ from its own location has a technical problem, priced separately (M4L4) and a sign the client has outgrown the methods (M4L5).
- No promises of results.

# Main frameworks
**Agency roadmap (M1L4):** rank map for primary category + city every other week, three steps, Chamber of Commerce, check the map; below target add 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month; still below, Core 30; at target, geographic relevance. Every new page gets a decent link.

**Three-step low competition method (M1L5, done in Module 2):**
1. GBP audit and fix: primary category matched to real searches (left alone if ranking well), up to 10 relevant categories, services expanded with no duplicates, every field and attribute filled.
2. GBP landing page audit and fix: primary category + city in title tag (brand last, 60 characters or less) and H1, NAP matching the GBP, LocalBusiness schema, real area content, map and reviews embeds, click-to-call.
3. Super (verified) citations: Apple Maps, Bing Places and others, free by hand or via LeadSnap (paid).

**Rank map targets:**
| Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Before any change | Baseline. Save it. |
| 20 to 40% top 3 green | Target reached, usually within 1 to 2 months in low to medium competition |
| Steady growth to 30, 40 or 50% | Three steps are enough. Stay the course. |
| Stuck at 10 to 15% after 8 to 10 weeks | Market needs Core 30 |
| 20 to 40% reached during Core 30 | Move to geographic relevance |

**Core 30 (Module 3):** a page for every GBP category and service, linked the way the GBP is organized (home = primary category + city, category pages, service pages). URL structure does not matter; internal links do. Map the GBP, crawl with Screaming Frog, run the gap analysis in Claude, verify every "missing" page, draft with the category or service prompt, edit by hand, publish with the linking structure. Most businesses need 15 to 25 new pages.

**Client acquisition channels (M4L1 to M4L3):**
| Channel | Cost | Speed and scale | Core move |
|---|---|---|---|
| Facebook Ads | $20 to $30 a day minimum | Fastest; claimed 97 clients in six months | Call-based funnel; no guarantees |
| Local networking | Time only | High quality, limited scale | Free rank map plus a few fixes; no pitch |
| Content marketing | Time only | Broad reach, months to years | Avatar, binge sessions, educational content |
| Referrals | Not covered | Not covered | Named only |

**Scope-based pricing (M4L4):** cost every setup step (Claude project or GPT, info sheet, GBP audit, landing page audit, LeadSnap) and every per-article step (writing, schema, images, links, PBN link, developer, QC, internal link updates to old content); add a 50 to 70% gross margin; month one setup plus about five articles, then nine a month; price complex technical work separately; offer good, better, best; present scope and value before price.

**Three outgrow signs (M4L5):** plateau despite proper work; very competitive market; complex technical issues (500+ pages ranking poorly at their own location).

# Master checklist (condensed)
- **Measure:** rank map baseline for primary category + city (or "near me"), tracked every 1 to 2 weeks; `site:` counts for top 3 and client; dated change log.
- **GBP:** primary category right; up to 10 secondary categories; 20 to 30 services, no duplicates; every field, attribute, special hours and https social link filled; posts, photos, reviews, Q&A; client approval first.
- **Landing page:** title tag and H1 with primary category + city; exact NAP on page and footer; click-to-call; LocalBusiness schema; real area content; map and reviews embeds; keep ranking content.
- **Citations and trust:** verified profiles (Apple Maps, Bing Places); Bing business profile; identical details; Chamber of Commerce; 1 to 2 local links per month while below target.
- **Decision point:** at about two months, compare green coverage to 20 to 40%. No random tactics.
- **Core 30:** trigger met; fundamentals ruled out; pages tied to real GBP categories and services; "Miami vs Denver" and fact checks; links mirror the GBP.
- **Geographic relevance:** only after the target is reached.
- **Outgrow check:** plateau, competitive market, large site ranking poorly at its own location.
- **Winning clients:** gap analysis skill first; channel chosen by budget; any paid channel approved; no guarantees; no pitch; educational content linking piece to piece.
- **Pricing:** every step costed including QC and internal link updates; 50 to 70% margin; technical work separate; three profitable options.

# How to use this at TAG
- Same order for [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub): rank map baseline, three-step audit, trust links, then Core 30 only if the two-month test says so.
- Rank maps: check what grid rank tracking TAG already has in [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas) before considering LeadSnap.
- Alphalete: fundamentals before Core 30 (only 3 of 244 pages indexed in June 2026 per Kim's memory; see [GSC Indexing Tracker](lib:brain-gsc-indexing-tracker), [Google Search Console](lib:brain-google-search-console)). It also matches the M4L5 "complex technical issues" sign, which M4L4 says to scope separately from content.
- Summit AZ maps closely to Core 30: the Module 3 examples are plumbing.
- Update older posts with internal links whenever a new blog goes live (M4L4), as a copy-paste list for Kim; link client blog posts into a path (M4L3). See [SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards).
- Acquisition and pricing are Scott's decisions; the free rank map offer and cost list are options Kim can bring him.
- Read-only rule: all GBP, website, citation and ad changes are recommendations for Kim to apply.

# Open questions and caveats
- **Contradictions:** green target 20 to 40% (audio) vs 30 to 40% (M1L4 slides); whether Chamber and local links come before Core 30; tracking every other week vs every 1 to 2 weeks; geographic relevance as service area content vs neighborhoods and landmarks; plateau number 5 to 10% (M4L5 audio) vs 10 to 15%; technical threshold 450, 500 or 500+ URLs; four channels named, three taught.
- **Claims to verify before repeating to clients:** the 70 to 80% success rate in markets under 500,000; ChatGPT relies on Bing's index; LeadSnap can skip verification; all timelines; the lobby test numbers; URL structure not mattering; "Core 30" as a name never explained; 97 clients in six months from Facebook Ads; the 1,000-subscriber five-figure YouTube story; 50 to 70% margin as standard (no actual prices shown).
- **Paid tools and costs needing Kim's OK:** LeadSnap ($20 per month per location for citations, as stated); Screaming Frog (free up to 500 URLs); GMB Everywhere (price not stated); Chamber of Commerce and charity sponsorships; Facebook ad spend ($20 to $30 a day minimum); PBN links (confirm with Scott); the Pro group (two-prompt content process, YouTube scripting prompts, Core 30 workflows, weekly huddles).
- **Resources not in the videos (course page):** Prompt Library local link prompt, offsite analysis prompt, GBP Review document, questionnaire, service sorting prompt, landing page writing prompt, Core 30 PowerPoint template, gap analysis prompt, category and service page prompts, the locked Facebook Ads classroom, and the written Pricing Framework lesson text.
